negative_findings.description: No Big Four Slovenia publication dedicated to Slovenian banking or payments was found. Searches in Slovenian for 'Deloitte KPMG EY PwC Slovenija bančništvo raziskava plačilni sistemi' returned only generic service pages, firm directory entries and KPMG transparency reports from 2015/2016.
negative_findings.result_summary: Slovenia-specific Big Four banking/payments studies appear not to exist as standalone local publications; Slovenia is covered only as a country line inside regional (CEE) studies.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Coverage of consultancy views on Slovenian banking must be built from regional CEE studies (Deloitte CEE Banking M&A, Raiffeisen CEE Banking Sector Report) rather than local outputs; expectations of local deliverables should be reset.

negative_findings.description: Full-text credit opinions and BICRA reports from Moody's, S&P and Fitch on Slovenian banks are behind subscription platforms (Moody's.com login, RatingsDirect, Fitch account).
negative_findings.result_summary: Only headlines, rating grades and outlooks are freely observable; report bodies are not.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's highest-value forward-looking content is licensable, not scrapable. A budget/licensing decision, or systematic reliance on issuer IR mirrors and newswires, is required.

negative_findings.description: A Fitch Ratings entity page for Slovenian issuers could not be confirmed from search results; the URL recorded in the candidate list is an inferred pattern, not an observed link.
negative_findings.result_summary: Fitch coverage of Slovenian banks is well evidenced through media and issuer statements, but no verified Fitch-hosted landing URL was obtained in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream verification must resolve the correct Fitch entity/issuer URLs before the source is treated as collectable; failure to fetch should not be read as absence.

negative_findings.description: No established Slovenian-language term was found for 'transparency exercise' or 'supervisory banking statistics'; Slovenian coverage of EBA/ECB datasets appears to use the English names untranslated.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language querying for these EU datasets yields no distinct sl vocabulary to exploit.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For EU supervisory datasets, English-only querying is adequate and sl querying adds no recall — but this must be documented rather than silently assumed.

negative_findings.description: No public list of equity analysts covering NLB (the only listed Slovenian bank, LSE GDR + Ljubljana) with their target prices was located in this pass; searches surfaced only Raiffeisen's sector report.
negative_findings.result_summary: Analyst-coverage metadata for NLB was not found openly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sell-side consensus is a valuable forward-looking signal; a follow-up should check NLB's own IR site for an 'analyst coverage' page, which many listed banks publish.

coverage_gaps.description: Smaller Slovenian banks and savings banks (SKB/OTP-merged entities, Gorenjska banka/AIK, Addiko Bank Slovenia, Delavska hranilnica, Sparkasse) were not individually checked for rating-agency coverage.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run per-issuer searches combining each bank's official name with 'bonitetna ocena' and 'rating' to map which second-tier banks are rated at all.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank annual-report auditor's opinions (revizorjevo mnenje / revizijsko poročilo) inside Slovenian bank annual reports were not harvested, nor was the mapping of which Big Four firm audits which Slovenian bank.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extract the auditor block and key audit matters from each bank's latest annual report PDF and cross-check against ANR registers and Big Four transparency reports.

coverage_gaps.description: IT/operational and cyber risk assessments of Slovenian banks (DORA readiness, ICT risk in SREP, ECB cyber stress test results with a Slovenia line) were not searched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Dedicated queries on ECB DORA/ICT-risk supervisory outputs and EBA ICT risk reporting filtered for Slovenia, plus Big Four DORA advisory material aimed at the SI market.

coverage_gaps.description: Domestic academic/think-tank assessors of the banking sector (University of Ljubljana Faculty of Economics, IMAD/UMAR, Bank Association of Slovenia analyses) were not covered as third-party analysts.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a query pass for 'Združenje bank Slovenije analiza', 'UMAR bančni sektor', and EF UL research on Slovenian banking.

coverage_gaps.description: Licensed terminal/aggregator routes to agency research (Bloomberg, LSEG, Alacra, CBonds) were only glimpsed via alacrastore.com search hits and not assessed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assess Alacra/CBonds per-report purchase pricing as a cheaper alternative to full agency subscriptions for occasional Slovenian bank reports.

brief: Third-party assessment of Slovenian banks splits cleanly into three tiers. Tier one is EU supervisory and resolution data — EBA transparency exercise and the new EDAP portal, ECB Supervisory Banking Statistics (Slovenia is an explicit SI country dimension, repeatedly the EU's highest net interest margin), SRB MREL outputs and IMF Article IV — all open, machine-readable and the backbone of any Slovenia bank benchmark. Tier two is the rating agencies (Moody's, S&P/BICRA, Fitch, plus Scope and DBRS on the sovereign): rich and forward-looking but largely paywalled, so in practice they are collected through issuer IR mirrors (NLB Group ratings page, OTP banka ratings page) and Slovenian/regional media (RTV SLO's 'bonitetna ocena' archive, SeeNews). Tier three is the audit and consultancy layer: no Slovenia-specific Big Four banking study appears to exist, so Slovenia is best tracked as a country line in Deloitte's CEE Banking M&A Study and Raiffeisen Research's CEE Banking Sector Report, while the audit angle is best worked through the regulator ANR's public registers and oversight decisions plus Big Four transparency reports. Priority follow-ups are the auditor-to-bank mapping and ICT/operational-risk supervisory outputs, neither of which this pass covered.
